narrativeReportMd:
# Flag R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No R4-valid Flag instance pattern was found that becomes invalid solely because of a local Flag element change in R6. The material risks are mostly R6-to-R4 conversion and runtime/code-generation risks: `Flag.status` is no longer mandatory, `Flag.subject` and `Flag.author` accept additional reference target types, and R6 adds `Flag.supportingInfo`.

## Scope
The analysis compared the local R4 4.0.1 and R6 6.0.0-ballot4 core `StructureDefinition/Flag` files, the relevant local value sets/code systems, package indexes, package metadata, the assignment manifest row, and the R4 `flag-detail` extension because R6 explicitly says `supportingInfo` replaces it. Inherited `Resource`/`DomainResource` changes are excluded from findings.

## Main migration themes
The most important migration theme is that R6 broadens what a valid Flag can look like. R6 can omit the modifier `status`, can point `subject` at `RelatedPerson` or `PractitionerRole`, can point `author` at `RelatedPerson`, and can carry supporting detail in a core element. These are not old-valid/new-invalid breaks, but R4 receivers and R4-shaped generated models need explicit handling.

## Highest-impact findings
`Flag.status` is the highest-risk change because code and workflows commonly assume a required modifier status. `Flag.subject` is also high impact for down-conversion because the required subject can now be a type R4 did not allow.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is recommended for policy decisions around missing `status` and for any R6 Flag whose required `subject` is a `RelatedPerson` or `PractitionerRole`, because a faithful R4 replacement is not generally computable from the Flag alone.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Most R6 changes are additive or widening. They improve expressivity, but backward compatibility would have been stronger if status had remained required or if R6-only expressivity had been carried by extensions/profiles rather than changing the base resource shape.

## Follow-up analysis
Base resource changes, Flag search parameters, the external flag-category terminology, and target resource analyses should be handled by their respective artifact reports.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: No local `Flag` change appears to make an R4-valid instance invalid in R6. The top concerns are optional `status`, widened `subject` targets, and R6-only `supportingInfo`; the main uncertainty is rationale and terminology context not present in local change notes.
summary.migrationThemesMd: R6 widens the model rather than narrowing it. Forward migration from R4 to R6 is mostly permissive, but R6-to-R4 conversion must handle missing required R4 `status`, reference targets that R4 did not permit, and the new `supportingInfo` element. Generated classes, validators, and business rules should be retested for absent status and widened reference unions.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural changes because both assigned StructureDefinitions were present and directly compared. Confidence is lower for design rationale and terminology nuance because official diffs, ballot notes, full narrative pages, and terminology expansions were not available locally.

findings.title: Flag.status changed from mandatory to optional

binding.description: Indicates whether this flag is active and needs to be displayed to a user, or whether it is no longer needed or was entered in error.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The local complete R4 and R6 `CodeSystem/flag-status` files contain the same three codes: `active`, `inactive`, and `entered-in-error`. No terminology expansion was generated.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, every valid Flag had one status value from the required Flag Status value set.

newState.summary: R6 permits `Flag.status` to be omitted and says omission means the status is unknown.

binding.description: Indicates whether this flag is active and needs to be displayed to a user, or whether it is no longer needed or was entered in error.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The value set version changed to 6.0.0-ballot4, but local compose still includes `http://hl7.org/fhir/flag-status` and the local complete CodeSystem has the same codes and definitions.

flags.isModifierReason: This element is labelled as a modifier because it is a status element that contains status entered-in-error which means that the resource should not be treated as valid

semanticText.comment: This element is labeled as a modifier because the status contains codes that mark the resource as not currently valid.
semanticText.meaningWhenMissing: When status is not valued, it means the status is unknown.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6, a Flag without `status` is valid and has an explicitly documented unknown status.

facts.newValue: When status is not valued, it means the status is unknown.

facts.note: Binding strength and local code set appear unchanged.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not an R4-to-R6 validation break because R6 is less restrictive. It is high impact for runtime and down-conversion because `status` is a modifier and was mandatory in R4. R6 instances with no status cannot be valid R4 Flags unless a converter invents a status value or carries the unknown state outside the base R4 element.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Flag display and suppression decisions often depend on whether a flag is active, inactive, or entered in error. Treating an omitted R6 status as active, inactive, or ignorable without policy review can change clinical or operational behavior.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow a Flag whose workflow status is not known.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `Flag.status` 1..1 and represent unknown status explicitly, for example with a new status code, but this only partially avoids breakage.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: R6 explicitly needs to represent a Flag whose status is unknown. Making the modifier element optional is disruptive for generated models, runtime logic, and R6-to-R4 conversion, but the best less-breaking base design is only partial. Adding an `unknown` required-binding code would keep the element present, yet still break enum-oriented code and would not be valid R4 without a policy or extension.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The strongest less-breaking base alternative would retain R4's `1..1` cardinality and add an explicit `unknown` status value. That would preserve the old required shape and avoid null-handling surprises, but it would introduce a new required-binding code, still require R6-to-R4 handling, and might be semantically weaker because unknown status is not itself an active/inactive/error workflow state. Extension or profile handling would be a mitigation rather than a uniform base R6 design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: A required unknown status preserves nullability assumptions but still changes the required code set, remains hard to down-convert to R4, and may conflate unknown state with workflow state.

evidence.detail: R6 adds explicit semantics for an omitted status.
evidence.quote: When status is not valued, it means the status is unknown.

evidence.detail: The compared local complete CodeSystems contain the same status codes and definitions.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 example is intentionally minimal and illustrates the omitted `status`. A down-converter must not blindly choose `active`; the migration example only shows the shape after a policy decision has supplied a value.

findings.narrativeMd: `Flag.status` moved from required to optional. Because the element remains a modifier, code that previously treated status as always present must now handle an explicit unknown/missing state. The change is permissive for R4 data moving forward to R6, but disruptive for R6 data moving back to R4 and for generated APIs that model status as non-null.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid Flag with `status` remains valid with respect to this element in R6. A valid R6 Flag without `status` is not a valid base R4 Flag because R4 requires `status`. Strict R4 validators will reject the omission, and generated R4 models or business logic may fail or silently misclassify the flag if a converter supplies a default without review.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Forward migration can retain existing R4 status values. R6 consumers should update validation, generated models, nullability annotations, enum switches, and display logic to handle missing status as unknown. Down-conversion to R4 requires a documented policy: reject such records, manually review them, populate a defensible status, or carry unknown status in an extension/profile-specific mechanism.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The need to represent unknown status is understandable, but making a modifier element optional is a broad base-resource change. A backward-compatible alternative would keep the element required and represent unknown explicitly, or use an extension/profile for exceptional unknown cases. Those alternatives preserve R4 cardinality expectations but still require downstream systems to understand the new semantics.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is recommended before selecting a default R4 status for omitted R6 status because the wrong choice can change whether a warning is displayed or ignored.

findings.title: Flag.subject can now reference RelatedPerson or PractitionerRole

oldState.summary: R4 required `Flag.subject` to reference one of eight target resource types.

semanticText.definition: The patient, location, group, organization, or practitioner etc. this is about record this flag is associated with.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, the required subject could not be a `RelatedPerson` or `PractitionerRole`.

newState.summary: R6 keeps `Flag.subject` required but adds `RelatedPerson` and `PractitionerRole` as allowed targets.

semanticText.definition: The patient, related person, location, group, organization, or practitioner etc. this is about record this flag is associated with.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 broadens the required subject reference to include `RelatedPerson` and `PractitionerRole`.

facts.oldValue: The patient, location, group, organization, or practitioner etc. this is about record this flag is associated with.
facts.newValue: The patient, related person, location, group, organization, or practitioner etc. this is about record this flag is associated with.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances do not become invalid in R6 because the target set only widened. The risk is high for down-conversion because `subject` is mandatory: an R6 Flag about a `RelatedPerson` or `PractitionerRole` has no base R4-allowed subject target with the same meaning. R4 validators and generated reference-type unions can reject such instances.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The subject identifies what the warning is about. Substituting a patient or practitioner for a related person or role can change the meaning and routing of the flag.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow flags to be directly about a related person or a practitioner acting in a role.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable because this is target widening; all R4-valid subject targets remain valid in R6.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of allowing a Flag to be about a RelatedPerson or PractitionerRole is plausible and the base R6 change does not invalidate R4 instances. The breakage is in R6-to-R4 representability and in implementations with closed target allow-lists, not in the R4-to-R6 base instance shape.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because R6 only adds allowed `subject` targets, there is no R4-to-R6 base-design break to avoid: existing R4 references remain within the R6 target set. Keeping the R4 target list and using extensions or profiles for RelatedPerson and PractitionerRole would reduce R6-to-R4 friction, but that is a compatibility mitigation with poorer core interoperability, not a `Yes` alternative under the calibration rules.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R4 down-conversion may need local policy, but extension or profile workarounds are mitigations rather than backward-compatible base-design alternatives for an R4-preserving widening.

evidence.detail: R4 target profiles exclude RelatedPerson and PractitionerRole.
R6 target profiles include RelatedPerson and PractitionerRole.

examples.examplesMd: The example is valid only if the referenced resource conforms to the stated target type. Its purpose is to show the R6-only target profile, not a complete clinical scenario.

findings.narrativeMd: `Flag.subject` remains required but its allowed reference targets widened. R6 Flags can now be directly about `RelatedPerson` or `PractitionerRole`; R4 base Flag could not express those as the required subject. The change is additive for R6 but can surprise R4 validators, generated models, and conversion logic.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old R4 subjects remain inside the R6 target set. However, an R6 Flag whose required subject is `RelatedPerson` or `PractitionerRole` is not valid against R4 target-profile constraints. Because the element is mandatory, a converter cannot simply omit it; it must either reject the instance or choose a semantically different allowed target with human or profile-specific rules.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Forward migration needs no transform for existing R4 targets. R6-capable code should update generated reference unions, validation allow-lists, and display/routing logic for the two new subject types. Down-conversion should flag these cases for review and avoid substituting a related patient, practitioner, or organization unless a local mapping rule proves the substitution is safe.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Adding targets is less disruptive than replacing the element, but it still creates R6 instances that R4 cannot represent. A profile or extension could have preserved base R4 compatibility, at the cost of making the broader subject semantics non-core and less discoverable.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is recommended for down-conversion because the correct R4 substitute, if any, depends on the referenced resource and business context.

findings.title: Flag.author can now reference RelatedPerson

oldState.summary: R4 author could reference Device, Organization, Patient, Practitioner, or PractitionerRole.

semanticText.definition: The person, organization or device that created the flag.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed several author types but not `RelatedPerson`.

newState.summary: R6 adds RelatedPerson as an author target.

semanticText.definition: The person, organization or device that created the flag.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 can identify a related person as the creator of the flag.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The target set widened, so existing R4 authors remain allowed. R6 instances with `author` pointing to `RelatedPerson` are not valid base R4 Flags. Because `author` is optional, a lossy down-converter could omit it, but that loses provenance about who created the flag.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Author is not a modifier, but losing or changing it can affect audit, accountability, or workflow routing.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent flags created by related persons such as caregivers or family members.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable because this is target widening; every R4-valid author target remains valid in R6.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding RelatedPerson is consistent with the author definition and supports caregiver or family-member authorship. Since `author` only widens and is optional, the R4-to-R6 base compatibility impact is limited; the meaningful risk is downstream conversion or strict generated target unions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible base alternative is needed for preserving R4 instances because the R6 target set is a superset of R4's. Keeping RelatedPerson authors solely in an extension would preserve an R4-shaped base model for down-conversion, but it would fragment a plausible core authoring case and is not counted as a backward-compatible base-design alternative for this additive widening.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 conversion of a RelatedPerson author can lose provenance, but extension/backport handling is migration guidance rather than a less-breaking base R6 design.

examples.examplesMd: This illustrates an R6 author target that R4 validators would reject for `Flag.author`.

findings.narrativeMd: `Flag.author` gained `RelatedPerson` as an allowed reference target. This supports caregiver- or family-authored flags but widens generated target unions and creates a down-conversion issue for R4 receivers.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid author references remain valid in R6. An R6 `RelatedPerson` author is not valid against R4's `Flag.author` target list. Since `author` is optional, dropping it can produce a valid R4 instance but loses information; replacing it with a patient or practitioner can be semantically wrong.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update R6 validation allow-lists and generated author reference types. For R6-to-R4 conversion, either retain the author in an extension, omit it with an explicit loss marker, or apply a local mapping only when the RelatedPerson can be safely represented by an R4-allowed target.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is a normal additive target widening. A backward-compatible alternative would use an extension for related-person authors, but that would fragment a plausible core authoring use case.

findings.title: R6 adds Flag.supportingInfo as a core element

oldState.summary: R4 base Flag had no `supportingInfo` element.
oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 Flag StructureDefinition ends its local element set at `Flag.author`; supporting detail was available through the separate `flag-detail` extension rather than a core element.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional repeating `Flag.supportingInfo` references to supporting clinical or diagnostic resources.

semanticText.short: Extra information to use in context of the flag
semanticText.definition: Additional information that may be relevant to the flag, such as why the flag was created or how to guide management of the flag.
semanticText.comment: Flag.supportingInfo replaced the extension http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/flag-detail in R6. In previous versions, using this extension is correct, not the R6 version extension.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 turns supporting detail into a first-class optional element and documents its relationship to the prior `flag-detail` extension.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Optional additions do not make old R4 instances invalid in R6. They do affect strict R4 parsers and validators because `supportingInfo` is an unknown element in R4. R6-to-R4 conversion is usually possible by mapping to the R4 `flag-detail` extension, but that requires an explicit transform and receiver support for the extension.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Supporting information may explain why a safety flag exists or how it should be managed. Dropping it can reduce clinical context even though it is not a modifier.

justification.inferredGoal: Promote commonly used supporting-detail information from an extension into the core Flag resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable because `Flag.supportingInfo` is an optional additive R6 element and does not make R4-valid Flags invalid in R6.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 comment says `supportingInfo` replaces the prior `flag-detail` extension, so the inferred goal is to standardize commonly used supporting context as core Flag content. That is a reasonable R6 goal and the addition is optional, so it does not create an R4-to-R6 base validation break.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The apparent alternative of continuing to rely on `flag-detail` should not be scored as `Yes` here. It can be an R6-to-R4 transform or backport path, but the finding is an optional additive core element; R4 instances without the element remain valid in R6. Avoiding the new element would preserve R4-shaped wire content but would also leave important supporting details outside the R6 base model.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Continuing to use the R4 `flag-detail` extension helps down-conversion but is a migration/backport strategy, while a core element improves R6 discoverability and validation.

evidence.detail: No R4 local element with id `Flag.supportingInfo` was present.
R6 adds optional repeating `Flag.supportingInfo` as Reference to seven target profiles.
evidence.quote: Condition; Procedure; AllergyIntolerance; Observation; RiskAssessment; DocumentReference; DiagnosticReport

evidence.detail: R4 includes a `flag-detail` extension for Flag whose value is a Reference to Resource.
evidence.quote: Points to the Observation, AllergyIntolerance or other record that provides additional supporting information about this flag.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example maps one R6 `supportingInfo` reference to the R4 `flag-detail` extension. Multiple R6 entries would require multiple extension repetitions.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds `Flag.supportingInfo` to carry references that explain or guide management of the flag. The R6 definition explicitly says this replaces the older `flag-detail` extension. This is an additive R6 feature, not a forward validation break, but untransformed R6 JSON will not validate as R4 because R4 has no such core element.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances without `supportingInfo` remain valid in R6. R6 instances containing `supportingInfo` are invalid as base R4 unless transformed. A lossless R4 representation is plausible using the R4 `flag-detail` extension, because that extension can repeat on Flag and has a `valueReference`; however, systems that do not preserve or understand the extension may lose the supporting context.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Forward migration may optionally transform existing R4 `flag-detail` extensions into R6 `supportingInfo` when the value is a compatible reference. Down-conversion should map each R6 supportingInfo reference to one R4 `flag-detail` extension or document loss if the receiver cannot accept extensions. Tests should cover zero, one, and multiple supportingInfo references.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The compatible alternative was to continue using the extension. R6 chose a core element, likely to improve standardization and discoverability. That choice is reasonable but requires explicit cross-version transforms.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, derivation, abstract flag, and `DomainResource` base definition match. The R6 counterpart is present in the expected path.
No R4 local Flag element was removed or renamed. R6 adds `Flag.supportingInfo`, which is reported as a finding.
All local cardinalities are unchanged except `Flag.status` minimum cardinality decreasing from 1 to 0, which is reported as a finding.
Non-reference datatype codes for existing local elements are unchanged. Reference target additions on `subject` and `author`, and the new `supportingInfo` reference element, are reported as findings.

Binding strengths and canonical value-set URLs for `status`, `category`, and `code` are stable. `status` value-set version changed, but the local complete flag-status CodeSystem has the same codes; SNOMED and external THO expansions were not performed.
No local Flag-specific invariant was added, removed, or strengthened. Existing local elements retain only the common `ele-1` constraint. Inherited `dom-*` changes are out of scope.
No fixed value, pattern, or default value constraint was found on local Flag elements in either version.
No local maxLength, minValue, maxValue, or regex limit changes were found.
`Flag.status` remains a modifier with the same modifier reason. No other local Flag element became a modifier.
Summary flags on existing local elements are unchanged. The new `supportingInfo` element is not marked summary.
No local slicing was found on Flag elements in either StructureDefinition.
No choice element rename, primitive-type replacement, or element move was detected. Serialization risk is limited to the new R6 element and widened reference targets reported in findings.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Artifact metadata changed from draft/trial-use to active/normative
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: This changes conformance metadata rather than instance shape. It does not by itself make R4 instances invalid or create a new R6 element.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Governance and procurement processes may treat normative/active resources differently, but validators and serializers should focus on the structural changes reported separately.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Flag Status value-set version changed but local code set appears unchanged
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The required binding remains required and composes from the same CodeSystem. The local complete CodeSystem concepts are the same three codes with the same definitions.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Regenerate terminology artifacts against the R6 value-set version, but no status code remapping was identified from the local packages.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Identifier definition now says author instead of performer
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The element name, type, cardinality, summary flag, and requirements are unchanged. The text appears to align wording with `Flag.author` rather than changing validation semantics.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Documentation and generated comments may change, but stored identifiers do not need a structural transform.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: Inherited `dom-*` constraint expression and metadata differences appear in the Flag snapshot but are base-artifact changes and should be assessed in the DomainResource report.
R6 `Flag.supportingInfo` explicitly replaces the earlier `flag-detail` extension. Cross-version migration guidance depends on the extension's availability and receiver support.
New Flag reference targets should be checked in their own reports for independent R4-to-R6 breaking changes before assuming referenced content can be exchanged safely.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The analysis used local computable definitions but not an official R4-to-R6 diff, Jira issue, or ballot change rationale. Structural confidence is high, but justification assessments are partly inferred.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review official HL7 change proposals, ballot reconciliation notes, or generated comparison pages for Flag.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No terminology server expansion was run. Direct comparison of the complete local `flag-status` CodeSystem was sufficient for the required status binding, but `flag-code` depends on SNOMED CT and `flag-category` depends on an external THO CodeSystem absent from the R6 core package.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run version-specific terminology expansions for `ValueSet/flag-status`, `ValueSet/flag-code`, and `ValueSet/flag-category` with the appropriate terminology packages.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The new input is an R6 ballot build, not necessarily the final published R6 specification. Ballot content can still change.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Repeat the comparison against the final R6 core package when available.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The analysis did not recursively assess breaking changes in newly referenced target resources such as `RelatedPerson` and `PractitionerRole`.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Combine this report with the assigned reports for those target resources and for the `Reference` datatype.
